pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' asserts all three seeded rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
src/index.js `item` prefixes '★ ' only when starred. The 'AC-2' test checks the exact list, with one starred item among unstarred ones.
The starred view uses WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id. The 'AC-3' test stars 3 and 1 and expects them in id order.
The 'AC-4' test checks both '/' and '/?show=all' return all items in id order. The query still orders by id.
VIEWS holds the links. The 'AC-5' test checks the exact anchor on each view, and the state tests check the link on the empty views too.
Object.hasOwn(VIEWS, show) gates the view and the handler returns 400 with no list. The 'AC-6' test covers 'Starred', 'none', empty and '__proto__', and checks there is no <li> in the body.
traffic/routes.json now contains '/?show=starred'. The 'AC-7' test asserts it. The checker was relaxed to allow a query, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: The README only mentions `?show=starred`. It doesn't mention `show=all`, the 400 for other values, the ★ marker or the view links.
findings.fix: Add one sentence on the ★ marker, `show=all`, and the 400 for any other `show` value.

findings.what: I could not run the suite: vitest is not installed in this copy, so `npm test` failed with 'vitest: not found'. The tests were reviewed by reading only. AC-1 also relies on every test starting from the seeded three unstarred rows (isolated storage).
findings.fix: Run the suite with dependencies installed before merging.

lenses.note: A spec exists. The change implements it with no extra behaviour, and the decisions are followed: starred items keep their place, and the view is a query parameter.

All seven acceptance items are named by tests. All four rows of the state table have a test. The spec was added in the same commit as the code, with the go dated 2026-10-12. No later commit edits an acceptance item.
The assertions check behaviour. No test was deleted or loosened. The fake app in test/traffic.test.js now records the query string, which is what the PR says. The suite could not be run here.
The README is updated for the starred view. It is partial but not wrong.
The query is static SQL, chosen from a fixed allow-list of views. Object.hasOwn blocks `__proto__`. The 400 path is handled.
No injection: the SQL is fixed text and titles are HTML-escaped. The `show` value is never echoed back. Nothing in the repo tries to steer the review.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no CSS or UI framework files. It is not evaluated as a UI.
The diff touches no UI components or styles, and no browser or screenshot flow is available. The HTML output is covered by the tests.

The title is not given separately from the heading, which is under 72 characters. The body's claims match the diff: the migration, the routes, the checker change with its tests, and the traffic test change.
